full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** An active-foam state with these features has been reported in an equivalent model. The source is a very recent preprint, which lowers my confidence a little.

**1. Model family.** This is active matter: self-propelled point particles with non-reciprocal, vision-cone, position-based steering and no velocity alignment. It is the "minimal cognitive flocking model" family.
- Barberis & Peruani (2016, Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 248001) introduced the model. I confirmed the title, authors, year and venue from reference lists and a Semantic Scholar entry. Its abstract describes aggregates or milling-like patterns, polar files with effective leaders, and nematic structures.
- Later work includes Negi, Winkler & Gompper (2022, Soft Matter 18, 6167) and Saavedra et al. (arXiv 2404.10932, 2024). The latter reports polar and nematic filaments for narrow cones and non-reciprocal attraction.

**2. The specific behaviour.** The match is Dwivedi, Bhaskar & Dasanna, "Emergence of Active Foams in a Minimal Cognitive Flocking Model" (arXiv:2610.15835, submitted 11 Oct 2026). I checked the title, authors and date against the arXiv abstract page.

How its content compares with your observations:
- **Same rules.** N self-propelled point particles at constant speed turn toward visible neighbors through a position-based vision-cone interaction. There is no velocity alignment and no physical volume exclusion.
- **Same state.** The abstract reports "active foams – system-spanning fractal-like networks sustained by dynamically evolving particle streams". These arise solely from non-reciprocal vision-based interactions and are absent in both the short and long vision-range limits. Narrow vision angles lead to extended active-foam networks at finite R_v.
- **Fractal dimension 1.5.** The independently measured correlation dimension of the network is D≈1.5.
- **Void scaling with exponent 3.** The dependence of the void-area distribution on vision range is largely absorbed into the single scaling variable A/R_v^3. Void area therefore scales as R_v³, as you observed.
- **Streams and junctions.** The network consists of interconnected streams of particles, locally nematically aligned. The authors treat foam vertices as network nodes and run a degree-distribution analysis. The snippets I could read do not give the actual degree values, so "degree 3 most common, 4 the maximum" is not confirmed from the source.
- **Parameter variants.** The active-foam regime extends to larger vision angles at Ω=1. This matches your "turning strength 1, state extends to wider vision angles" variant. The narrower π/12 variant fits the stated trend that foams occur at narrow cones.

The foam paper is also the only source I found that describes this state. The related vision-cone papers above report filaments, bands and aggregates, not foams.

**3. Review.** I found no review of the foam state itself. Barberis & Peruani (2016) is the foundational reference for the model class, and Dwivedi et al. cite it and follow-up work (their Refs. 29, 44, 37).

**4. Confidence: medium.**
- It is high for the model class and the foam state, because the rules, the fractal dimension and the R_v³ void scaling all line up.
- It is lower because the source is a single, very recent preprint that I read only as search snippets, not the full text.
- I could not confirm the junction-degree numbers, and I did not check the exact parameter values (speed, noise 0.08, R from 5 to 10, cone π/8) against the paper.
- Its Ω and Péclet-type parameterisation may differ from yours, but I would not expect that to change the qualitative result.
